runs.name: decide-lines
runs.command: thinkthen decide --lines --details --threshold 0.2:0.8 'Does the customer ask for a refund?' < messages.txt | jq -r '"\(.value)  \(.answer.probability)  \(.input)"'
runs.input:
Please refund my order. It arrived broken.
Thanks for the quick help yesterday!
I want to send this back.
runs.output:
true  0.99  Please refund my order. It arrived broken.
false  0.01  Thanks for the quick help yesterday!
null  0.54  I want to send this back.
runs.see: The refund request answers true and the thank-you note false. "I want to send this back." could mean an exchange or money back, so it lands inside the band as null at 0.54.

runs.name: decide-case
runs.input: I want to send this back.
runs.see: Sending it back could mean an exchange or money back. decide exits 3, and the case sends it to a person.

runs.name: decide
runs.command: thinkthen decide 'Does the customer ask for a refund?' < ticket.txt
runs.input:
I renewed once this morning, but my card shows two charges.
Please refund the duplicate.
runs.see: The ticket asks for a refund, so decide prints true and exits 0.

runs.name: decide-answer
runs.command: thinkthen decide --details 'Does the customer ask for a refund?' < ticket.txt | jq '.answer'
runs.input:
I renewed once this morning, but my card shows two charges.
Please refund the duplicate.
runs.see: The details put yes at 0.99 for this ticket.

runs.name: decide-means
runs.command: thinkthen decide 'Does the customer ask for a refund?' --true 'The customer asks for money back.' --false 'Anything else, such as a cancellation or a question.' < cancel.txt
runs.input: Please cancel my plan at the end of this month.
runs.see: A cancellation is not money back under these words, so decide says false and exits 1.
